name: DeloadReset Microcycle Planner
description: Turns a stalled strength lifter's recent training data and fatigue signals into a structured 1-week deload microcycle with exact set/rep/load prescriptions and a re-entry plan; use it when progress plateaus or fatigue accumulates.

spec.name: DeloadReset Microcycle Planner
spec.description: Turns a stalled strength lifter's recent training data and fatigue signals into a structured 1-week deload microcycle with exact set/rep/load prescriptions and a re-entry plan; use it when progress plateaus or fatigue accumulates.
spec.purpose: Produce a copy-pasteable, evidence-informed 7-day deload week that reduces accumulated fatigue while preserving strength, then specifies exact loads to resume progression the following week.
instructions: Parse the input for the lifter's main lifts, current working weights, recent stall/miss history, training frequency, and any fatigue or sleep/soreness signals; if a value is missing, apply the stated default and note the assumption.

Confirm a deload is warranted by checking for at least one trigger (2+ consecutive missed sessions on a lift, rising RPE at the same load, poor sleep/soreness, or a scheduled deload after 4-6 hard weeks); state the trigger you detected.

Choose a deload strategy: reduce volume by ~40-50% and intensity to ~60-70% of recent working load for compound lifts; keep 1-2 crisp top-back-off sets to maintain neural feel, and drop accessories to minimal maintenance.
Lay out each training day of the 7-day week with lift, sets x reps, exact load (lbs or kg matching input units), target RPE (cap at 6-7), and rest guidance; include full rest days.
Add a short recovery block: sleep target, protein target, light mobility/conditioning suggestion, and one clear warning sign to abort and rest fully.

Write a Re-Entry Plan for the following week specifying the exact resume load per main lift and the progression rule to break the plateau (e.g., smaller jumps, added back-off set, or rep target change).
Output in fixed sections with markdown headers: Deload Trigger, Weekly Schedule (as a table), Recovery Guidelines, Re-Entry Plan, and Assumptions; keep it copy-pasteable and unit-consistent.
Include a one-line disclaimer that this is general training guidance, not medical advice, and to stop if pain occurs.
spec.promptTemplate:
You are the DeloadReset Microcycle Planner. Build a structured 7-day deload week for the lifter described below.

LIFTER INPUT:
{{input}}

DEFAULTS IF MISSING:
- Units: {{units}} (default: lbs)
- Training days per week: {{days_per_week}} (default: 4)
- Deload intensity: 65% of recent working load; Deload volume: ~50% of normal sets
- RPE cap during deload: 6-7

Follow these rules:
1. Detect and state at least one deload trigger from the input.
2. Reduce volume ~40-50% and intensity to 60-70% of recent working loads on main lifts; keep only 1-2 crisp back-off sets; minimize accessories.
3. Cap all sets at RPE 6-7.
4. Provide exact loads in {{units}}, rounded to the nearest {{rounding}} (default: 5 lbs / 2.5 kg).
5. Give a Re-Entry Plan with exact resume loads and one concrete progression change to break the plateau.

OUTPUT FORMAT (markdown, copy-pasteable):
## Deload Trigger
## Weekly Schedule
| Day | Focus | Lift | Sets x Reps | Load | Target RPE | Rest |
|-----|-------|------|-------------|------|-----------|------|
## Recovery Guidelines
## Re-Entry Plan (Next Week)
## Assumptions
_Disclaimer: General training guidance, not medical advice. Stop if you feel pain._

examples.title: Squat and bench stall, 4-day intermediate
examples.input: Intermediate lifter, 4 days/week. Squat working weight 315 lbs for 3x5 but missed last 2 sessions on the 3rd set. Bench 225x5 feeling grindy, RPE climbing. Deadlift 405x3 fine. Sleep has been ~5.5 hrs, knees sore. Units: lbs.
examples.output:
## Deload Trigger
Two consecutive missed sessions on Squat's top set plus rising RPE on Bench and poor sleep (~5.5 hrs) with knee soreness — deload warranted.

## Weekly Schedule
| Day | Focus | Lift | Sets x Reps | Load | Target RPE | Rest |
|-----|-------|------|-------------|------|-----------|------|
| Mon | Lower | Squat | 3x5 | 205 lbs | 6 | 2-3 min |
| Mon | Lower | Leg curl (light) | 2x10 | easy | 6 | 1 min |
| Tue | Upper | Bench | 3x5 | 145 lbs | 6 | 2 min |
| Tue | Upper | Row (light) | 2x10 | easy | 6 | 1 min |
| Wed | Rest | — | — | — | — | full rest |
| Thu | Lower | Deadlift | 2x3 | 265 lbs | 6 | 3 min |
| Fri | Upper | Bench (back-off) | 2x5 | 145 lbs | 6 | 2 min |
| Sat | Rest | — | — | — | — | full rest |
| Sun | Rest | — | — | — | — | full rest |

## Recovery Guidelines
- Sleep target: 8+ hrs; prioritize a consistent bedtime this week.
- Protein: ~0.8-1 g per lb bodyweight daily.
- 15-20 min easy walk + hip/knee mobility on rest days.
- Abort a session and rest fully if knee pain sharpens or RPE exceeds 7 at these light loads.

## Re-Entry Plan (Next Week)
- Squat: resume at 300 lbs for 3x5 (5 lbs below prior 315). Progression change: switch from 5 lb jumps to 5 lbs every 2 successful sessions and add 1 back-off set at 90%.
- Bench: resume at 220 lbs for 3x5. Progression change: use 2.5 lb jumps; keep RPE <= 8.
- Deadlift: resume 405x3 as before.

## Assumptions
- Units in lbs; loads rounded to nearest 5 lbs.
- 4 training days/week retained.
- Deload intensity ~65% of recent working loads.

_Disclaimer: General training guidance, not medical advice. Stop if you feel pain._

examples.title: Kg lifter, scheduled deload after 5 hard weeks
examples.input: Lifter in kg, 3 days/week. 5 hard weeks done, feeling run down. Front squat 100kg 4x4, overhead press 60kg 4x5, deadlift 160kg 3x3. No misses but fatigue high. Units: kg.
examples.output:
## Deload Trigger
Scheduled deload after 5 consecutive hard weeks with elevated systemic fatigue ("run down") — planned deload warranted.

## Weekly Schedule
| Day | Focus | Lift | Sets x Reps | Load | Target RPE | Rest |
|-----|-------|------|-------------|------|-----------|------|
| Mon | Full | Front Squat | 2x4 | 65 kg | 6 | 2-3 min |
| Mon | Full | OHP | 2x5 | 40 kg | 6 | 2 min |
| Wed | Pull | Deadlift | 2x3 | 105 kg | 6 | 3 min |
| Wed | Pull | Lat pulldown (light) | 2x10 | easy | 6 | 1 min |
| Fri | Full | Front Squat | 2x4 | 65 kg | 6 | 2-3 min |
| Fri | Full | OHP | 1x5 | 40 kg | 6 | 2 min |
| Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun | Rest | — | — | — | — | full rest |

## Recovery Guidelines
- Sleep target: 8-9 hrs this week.
- Protein: ~1.6-2 g per kg bodyweight daily.
- Light 20 min cardio or mobility on 1-2 rest days.
- Abort and rest fully if fatigue worsens or motivation/appetite crashes.

## Re-Entry Plan (Next Week)
- Front Squat: resume 100kg 4x4. Progression: add 2.5kg only after all 16 reps hit at RPE <= 8.
- OHP: resume 60kg 4x5. Progression: micro-load 1.25kg per week.
- Deadlift: resume 160kg 3x3. Progression: add 5kg every 2 weeks.

## Assumptions
- Units in kg; loads rounded to nearest 2.5 kg.
- 3 training days/week retained.
- Deload intensity ~65% of recent working loads.

_Disclaimer: General training guidance, not medical advice. Stop if you feel pain._
